content: Dyck language completion: parse input tracking unmatched opening brackets in a stack (by type: <>, [], {}, etc.). To complete: emit closing brackets matching each open in reverse order (LIFO stack-pop order), one closing bracket per opening. Output only the completion fragment to append, not the full balanced string.

Dyck language matching (bracket balance/completion): Implement a stack-based algorithm that applies to all instances — iterate through the sequence, push opening brackets ({, [, <, () onto a stack, pop and verify when closing brackets (}, ], >, )) are encountered. At the end, close all remaining open brackets in reverse LIFO order, preserving spacing between tokens to match input format. Do not guess; apply this procedure systematically.

dyck_languages: solve by maintaining a stack of open brackets (type and position). Process the sequence left-to-right. At completion, close all remaining open brackets in LIFO order (last-opened-first-closed), matching bracket types exactly.
